title: Tenant attribution and quota enforcement for dedicated capacity billing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement reliable tenant-level attribution and quota enforcement for Dedicated capacity pools so that usage is correctly billed to the owning tenant, burst allowances are tracked separately, and SLA credit eligibility can be computed deterministically.

Background: Dedicated pools currently emit aggregate throughput metrics and a separate aggregated burst counter. This has created gaps during multi-tenant pools and transient reroutes: (1) per-tenant usage attribution is approximate, (2) quota enforcement is applied at the pool boundary rather than tenant boundary, and (3) calculating SLA credits requires cross-referencing multiple derived metrics which can be inconsistent during high churn.

Scope:
- Add deterministic tenant attribution to the serving path by propagating tenant_id and route_id into the metering shim and ensuring every token event is stamped with a tenant reference.
- Implement a per-tenant leaky-bucket meter that consumes from two buckets: reserved_throughput and burst_credits.
- Change enforcement semantics: when tenant reserved bucket is exhausted, allow consumption from burst_credits up to configured burst cap; block/queue requests only when both buckets are exhausted or when tenant-defined hard quota exceeded.
- Create a reconciliation pipeline that runs hourly to detect negative adjustments, duplicate events, and missed attributions; emit correction records for invoice adjustments and SLA credit decisions.
- Add auditable event stream for billing downstream consumers (BigQuery topic and daily partitioned table) and include fields needed for invoices and audit: tenant_id, pool_id, model_variant, route, tokens_generated, tokens_charged, bucket_used, request_id, timestamp.

Out of scope: invoicing UI changes and accounting ledger integration (will be separate ticket).

Success criteria:
- Per-tenant token attribution accuracy >= 99.95% vs headroom simulation for a 7-day sample workload.
- Quota enforcement operates at tenant-level with <= 200ms additional P50 latency on request path for meter checks.
- SLA credit calculation can be produced deterministically from hourly partitioned tables without manual reconstructions.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant ID is present on 100% of metered token events for dedicated pools
Per-tenant leaky-bucket meter enforces reserved and burst semantics and prevents overdraw in safety tests
Hourly reconciliation job detects and fixes event gaps with documented correction records
Playback/replay of 48 hours of production traffic into a staging pipeline reproduces billed totals within 0.05%
PRD + design spec linked and engineering runbook created for post-deploy monitoring
comments: 2025-01-15 - Connor Lee: Spike completed to measure added latency for stamping tenant_id in hot path. Measured P50 +120us, P99 +1.8ms in our microbench harness. Acceptable with optimizations to reduce allocations.
2025-01-22 - Mariana Gomez (PM): Confirmed priority due to upcoming enterprise customer audits. Requested SLA credit deterministic window be max 72 hours for backfill eligibility.

2025-01-29 - Security review note: propagated tenant_id is non-sensitive but pipeline must strip any PII from metadata. Confirmed with Security that KMS is not required for tenant_id field. See Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Dedicated+Attribution+Design

2025-02-03 - Connor Lee: Implemented leaky-bucket prototype and unit tests for reserved->burst handoff. Edge case: simultaneous multi-route fanout caused double-charge in naive implementation; fixed using idempotent request_id hashing.
2025-02-04 - Code review: PR feedback requested to add integration test that replays duplicate events and verifies reconciliation emits correction records. Assigned to ENG-22109-sub1 (subtask).

2025-02-06 - Aisha Patel: Added acceptance tests for hourly reconciliation and sample BigQuery schema. Next: schedule canary deploy to one non-production pool and run 72-hour shadow billing comparison against legacy pipeline.
